title: I just wanted to make a browser FPS. Now I have a map editor and I think I’m accidentally building my own engine
author: Ditex_Design
selftext:
I’m a solo dev making BLOCKRIFT, a fast arena FPS that runs in the browser (Three.js + Colyseus multiplayer).

At first I built maps by editing JSON by hand. That got painful fast, so I built a map editor. Then I needed a weapon tuner to fix gun sizes and hand positions. Then a UI editor. At this point it kind of looks like I’m starting to build my own engine for this game, and I’m not sure if that’s genius or a trap 😅

What the map editor does right now:

* 2D top-down planning, a 3D view, or a split view with both live
* Walls, low cover, crates, containers, ramps, stairs, doorways, window walls and spawn points
* A paint brush for walls, plus scale, rotate and snap
* Mirror, align, group, and copy/paste, so symmetric maps go fast
* Map themes (the video switches Industrial to Night)
* “Test with bots” to jump straight into a match on the map

The video is one real session, from an empty arena to a playable layout, with the building part sped up.

My long-term goal is for it to be good enough to recreate classic FPS maps. Later I might let players build their own.
